## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Merging is blocked by one defect. `Cache.set` stores keys without lower-casing them, but `get` always looks keys up in lower case, so any mixed-case key passed to `set` cannot be read back. The `DEFAULT_TTL` change and its comment match each other. The policy manifest lists no policy files.

## Critical
- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — `set` writes `self._store[key]` using the key exactly as given, but `get` (app/cache.py:17) looks up `key.lower()`. The comment at app/cache.py:14-15 says "every path into _store lower-cases the key first". With `c.set("Alpha", 1)`, the entry is stored under `"Alpha"`, and both `c.get("Alpha")` and `c.get("alpha")` return `None`. The new round-trip test at tests/test_cache.py:10-14 only calls `set` with the already-lowercase `"alpha"`, so it can't catch this. Could you change it to `self._store[key.lower()] = ...` and add a test that calls `set("Alpha", ...)`? — A caller that uses a mixed-case key loses every write: the value is never readable, and the stray entry stays in `_store` because only `get` removes expired entries, and only for the lower-cased key. This is the duplicate-entry problem the comment warns about.

## Strengths
- `test_entries_expire` (tests/test_cache.py:21-27) monkeypatches `time.monotonic`. app/cache.py calls it as `time.monotonic()` through the module, so the patch applies to both `set` and `get`. That makes the test exercise the expiry branch at app/cache.py:21-23 without timing flakiness.
- The `DEFAULT_TTL` comment at app/cache.py:7 was updated with the value at app/cache.py:8 and still matches it, and `test_default_ttl_is_five_minutes` pins the new value.
